name: Bluetooth Classic (RFCOMM, A2DP, HID)
plain: Pairs and talks to classic Bluetooth devices such as headsets, printers and car kits.
meaning: Classic links expose paired devices by name and address, and serial links can carry any data. iPhone apps cannot open raw Classic sockets, which blocks many hobby and industrial uses.

android.api_surface: BluetoothSocket (RFCOMM), BluetoothAdapter, A2DP and HFP profiles

ios.prompt_ui: No raw prompt; MFi program membership and Bluetooth prompt for accessories
ios.store_policy: MFi licence required to ship hardware
ios.note: No public RFCOMM sockets; only MFi accessories speak Classic to apps.

limits.headline: Can talk to headsets, printers and car kits on Android; iPhone allows only certified accessories
limits.user_action: You pair a headset, printer or car kit, then use the app with it
can: List paired devices by name and address (Android)
Open a serial style link and exchange any data (Android)
Use audio and hands free profiles with headsets and car kits
Connect to Apple certified (MFi) accessories on iPhone
cannot: Open raw Classic Bluetooth links on iPhone
Support many hobby and industrial gadgets on iPhone
Connect on Android 12 and later before you allow Nearby devices
limits.differs: Android lets apps open Classic links directly; iPhone limits Classic to MFi accessories and has no raw sockets.

story.what_it_is: The older Bluetooth that links to headsets, printers, car kits and card readers.
story.for_you: You pair a printer, a handheld scanner or a car kit and it just works. On iPhone only some certified accessories can use this link with apps. On Android the app can talk to many more devices.
story.for_makers: Classic Bluetooth carries audio and plain serial data, so it is used for receipt printers, card readers and car diagnostic tools. Android gives apps room to build with it. iPhone limits it to certified accessories.

use_cases.example: A shop's receipt printer pairs to the point of sale app and prints when a sale ends.
A car diagnostic dongle reads engine codes into a phone app.
Your car stereo pairs your phone for calls and music.
A warehouse handheld scanner sends barcodes to an inventory app.
A pulse oximeter or older medical gadget sends numbers to a health app.
A wireless game controller connects to a phone for a console style game.
A label printer prints parcel labels from a shipping app.

story.android_note: Android lets apps open Classic Bluetooth serial links to paired devices.
story.ios_note: iPhone has no public serial link for apps. Only certified accessories (MFi) can talk Classic Bluetooth to apps.

technical_bounds: iOS needs MFi membership for Classic accessories
Pairing happens in system UI on both OS

abuse: Silent device census of paired items
